guide.summary: Use a Notion public connection (OAuth 2.0) with only the Read content capability. Each customer authorizes the app and selects the pages to share through the OAuth page picker. Choose the installation scope at creation, since it cannot be changed later. Test with one representative workspace and a page you select during authorization. Do not request Insert content or Update content. Whether the app needs provider review or a Marketplace listing for customer rollout is not established by the supplied sources.

findings.title: Public connection OAuth fits customer workspaces
findings.detail: Notion documents public connections as OAuth connections that each authorizing user installs into their own workspace, with a per-user access token.

evidence.quote: A public connection is an OAuth connection that users install into their Notion workspaces. Unlike internal connections , which are scoped to a single workspace with a static token, public
connections follow the OAuth 2.0 protocol: each user who authorizes the connection receives their own access token, scoped to their workspace.

findings.title: Read content capability covers both read actions
findings.detail: Read content gives access to read existing content, including retrieving pages. Missing capabilities return 403.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to both requested read actions

evidence.quote: Read content : This capability gives a connection access to read existing content in a Notion workspace. For example, a connection with only this capability is able to call Retrieve
​ Errors The connection needs read content capabilities . Missing capabilities return 403 . A missing page or missing access returns 404 .

findings.title: Customers choose pages during authorization
findings.detail: Public connections use the OAuth page picker, where users choose which pages to grant access to during the authorization flow.

evidence.quote: Page access: Internal connections require workspace members to manually share pages via the “Add connections” menu. Public connections use the OAuth page picker, where users choose which pages to grant
access to during the authorization flow.

steps.title: Create public connection with Read content only
steps.detail: In the Developer portal, create a public connection with Read content only and the installation scope you confirmed. Then open the Configuration tab to get the client ID and secret.
steps.doneWhen: Connection exists with only Read content enabled, and the OAuth client ID and secret are available in the Configuration tab.

evidence.quote: How to create a public connection in the Developer portal
When you create a public connection, you also choose its installation scope — either Any workspace (Marketplace-eligible) or Selected workspaces only (not Marketplace-eligible).
4 After creation, visit the Configuration tab to retrieve your OAuth client ID and OAuth client secret . The client ID identifies your connection to Notion during the OAuth flow,

steps.appliesWhen: Installation scope is the confirmed choice; Any workspace is the fit for customers in unknown workspaces

steps.title: Implement authorization URL and code-to-token callback
steps.detail: Build the authorization URL with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code and owner=user. The callback exchanges the returned code at the token endpoint using Basic auth with client ID and secret. Do not implement write actions.
steps.doneWhen: Authorization URL and callback code are implemented, and the redirect URI is registered for the connection.

evidence.quote: HTML < a href = "https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize?owner=user&client_id=463558a3-725e-4f37-b6d3-0889894f68de&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fexample.com%2Fauth%2Fnotion%2Fcallback&response_type=code" > Add to Notion </ a >
To set up this step, retrieve the code from the redirect URI.
Authorization : Basic "$CLIENT_ID:$CLIENT_SECRET"

steps.title: Authorize a representative test workspace
steps.detail: As a developer test user in one test workspace, approve the connection in the OAuth picker. Select one test page you control, then confirm the callback receives a code and the token exchange returns an access token.
steps.doneWhen: Callback receives an authorization code and token exchange returns an access token scoped to the selected test page.

evidence.quote: ​ How users authorize a public connection
4 After the user approves, Notion redirects them to your redirect URI with a temporary authorization code.
5 Your connection exchanges the code for an access token, which is used for all subsequent API requests on behalf of that user.

fields: Access token (use only in the test environment)

steps.title: Test read of shared page titles
steps.detail: Call GET /v1/pages/{page_id} with the OAuth access token and Notion-Version 2026-03-11. Expected response: a page object whose properties include the title. Boundary check: request a page you did not select during authorization, expecting 404 for missing access. This is a read-only GET; do not run write calls.
steps.doneWhen: Selected page returns its title property, and the unselected page returns 404 with no writes made.

evidence.quote: --url https://api.notion.com/v1/pages/{page_id} \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
​ Errors The connection needs read content capabilities . Missing capabilities return 403 . A missing page or missing access returns 404 .

string[] Property names or IDs to include in each page's properties object. Other properties are left out. Repeat the parameter to pass more than one value, for example filter_properties=title&filter_properties=Status .

fields: PAGE_ID (selected test page; from the page URL)

steps.title: Test read of shared page content
steps.detail: Call GET /v1/pages/{page_id}/markdown with markdown_version=v2 and the OAuth access token. Expected response: markdown content of the selected page. Boundary check: request an unselected page, expecting 403 or 404 without any write effect. Use only GET requests.
steps.doneWhen: Selected page returns markdown content, and the unselected page is rejected without any write effect.

evidence.quote: Requirements Your connection must have read content capabilities on the target page in order to call this endpoint. To update your connection’s capabilities, navigate to the Developer portal , select
Set the markdown_version query parameter to v2 to get Notion-flavored Markdown instead. v2 is recommended. v1 is deprecated. It’s the default on current Notion-Versions. See Markdown versions .
curl --request GET \
--url https://api.notion.com/v1/pages/{page_id}/markdown \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \

preparation.title: Registration worksheet
preparation.text:
Create public connection with Read content only
In the Developer portal, create a public connection with Read content only and the installation scope you confirmed. Then open the Configuration tab to get the client ID and secret.
Fields: Installation scope, Capabilities: Read content only, OAuth client ID, OAuth client secret (store securely)

Implement authorization URL and code-to-token callback
Build the authorization URL with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code and owner=user. The callback exchanges the returned code at the token endpoint using Basic auth with client ID and secret. Do not implement write actions.
Fields: client_id, redirect_uri, OAuth client secret (environment variable)
